findings.text: You need a client ID and client secret from the Dev Dashboard.
findings.quote: You have your app's client ID and client secret from the Dev Dashboard.

findings.text: You must add your app's redirect URI to your app's settings in the Dev Dashboard or your shopify.app.toml file.
findings.quote: You've added your app's redirect URI to your app's settings in the Dev Dashboard, or to the [auth] section of your shopify.app.toml.

findings.text: You must know which access scopes your app requires.
findings.quote: You know which access scopes your app requires.

findings.text: The refresh token expires in 90 days.
findings.quote:
refresh_token_expires_in

Seconds until the refresh token expires (90 days).

findings.text: If the state parameter does not match the stored nonce, reject the request.
findings.quote: Compare the state parameter to the nonce you stored in step 1. If they don't match, reject the request.

findings.text: If the shop domain does not match the required pattern, the app must not send the authorization code to the host.
findings.quote: Confirm the shop parameter matches ^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9\-]*\.myshopify\.com$. Anchor the pattern at both ends. Without the trailing $, a value such as exampleshop.myshopify.com.attacker.example passes the check, and your app sends the authorization code to a host you don't control.

findings.text: Use client credentials grant if the app only acts on stores in your own organization.
findings.quote: If your app only acts on stores in your own Shopify organization, use the client credentials grant instead. It skips the merchant authorization flow.

findings.text: Construct the authorization URL and redirect the merchant to it.
findings.quote: Construct the authorization URL and redirect the merchant to it. Include a randomly generated state value (nonce) and store it so you can verify it in the next step.

findings.text: Validate the callback parameters after the merchant approves the app.
findings.quote: After the merchant approves your app, Shopify redirects to your redirect_uri with an authorization code and several query parameters. Validate all of them before exchanging the code.

findings.text: Exchange the authorization code for an offline access token.
findings.quote: Exchange the authorization code for one by sending a POST request to Shopify's token endpoint.

findings.text: Store the access token and refresh token securely.
findings.quote: Store the access_token and refresh_token securely on your backend, along with expires_in and refresh_token_expires_in so you know when each token expires.

findings.text: You can use Shopify CLI to generate a new app project.
findings.quote: Use Shopify CLI to generate a new app project with everything you need.

findings.text: You can create an app using the Dev Dashboard.
findings.quote: Shopify CLI and the Dev Dashboard both work against the same app record, so you can create an app in either one.

findings.text: A custom app is installed directly by one organization without a listing or review.
findings.quote: A custom app takes the other path: one organization installs it directly, with no listing and no review.

findings.text: A Shopify App Store app is available to any merchant after passing review.
findings.quote: Publish your app in the Shopify App Store and any merchant can install it once it passes review.

findings.text: Submitting an app that does not meet requirements will result in a rejection and a lost review cycle.
findings.quote: Read the requirements before you submit, because a rejection costs you a full review cycle.

findings.text: You must have Node.js 18 or higher installed before you install your app.
findings.quote: Before you install, make sure you have Node.js 18 or higher.

findings.text: You can initialize a new app using the Shopify CLI.
findings.quote: Initialize new apps, themes, and headless storefronts in an instant with the latest Shopify CLI.

findings.text: Install the Shopify CLI globally on your machine.
findings.quote: Install Shopify CLI globally.

findings.text: Navigate to the directory where you want to create your app.
findings.quote: Navigate to the directory where you want to create your app.

findings.text: Run the shopify app init command to create a new app.
findings.quote: Run the second command to create a new app. Your app will be added as a new subdirectory.

findings.text: You must review the App Store requirements before submitting your app for public listing.
findings.quote: Review the App Store requirements and Theme Store requirements before you submit.

findings.text: The Customer Account API has a limit of 3,000 requests per minute per customer.
findings.quote:
Customer Account API

Cost points per store and customer, plus 3,000 requests per minute per customer

findings.text: Once a store has 500,000 product variants, no more than 10,000 new variants can be created per day.
findings.quote: Once a store has 500,000 product variants, no more than 10,000 new variants can be created per day, on any API.

findings.text: Input arguments that accept an array have a maximum size of 250.
findings.quote: Input arguments that accept an array have a maximum size of 250, on every Shopify API. Requests return an error if an input array exceeds 250 items.

findings.text: Pagination of arrays of objects caps at 25,000 objects.
findings.quote: Pagination of arrays of objects caps at 25,000 objects, and the cap applies to count queries too.

findings.text: You must choose between custom distribution for a specific merchant and public distribution for many merchants.
findings.quote: Building for a specific merchant: You'll typically use custom distribution. Building for many merchants: You'll use public distribution.

findings.text: You cannot change the distribution method after selecting it.
findings.quote: You can't change the distribution method after you select it.

findings.text: Public distribution requires registering for the Shopify App Store.
findings.quote: Public distribution also requires registering for the Shopify App Store, which has a one-time fee.

findings.text: Public distribution requires approval from Shopify.
findings.quote:
Approval required

Yes

findings.text: Theme app extensions have a 100 KB Liquid size limit.
findings.quote: Theme app extensions are subject to file and content size limits. If your app uses custom distribution, or your app has been granted Built for Shopify status in the Shopify App Store, then you can request an exception to the 100 KB Liquid size limit for a theme app extension.

findings.text: A privacy policy is required for your app listing.
findings.quote: Include a privacy policy (required) and consider adding other helpful links to your developer website such as FAQ page, changelog, support portal, tutorial, and additional documentation.

findings.text: Apps using APIs that will be deprecated within 90 days cannot be submitted.
findings.quote: Your app should use supported APIs only—apps using APIs that will be deprecated within 90 days can't be submitted.

findings.text: App names must be 30 characters or fewer.
findings.quote: Keep it short: Use 30 characters or fewer, which is the maximum length that an app name can be.

findings.text: App introduction text is limited to 100 characters.
findings.quote: Your app introduction (100 characters) should clearly highlight the benefits merchants can expect.

findings.text: App details text is limited to 500 characters.
findings.quote: In your app details (500 characters), describe functional elements and what makes your app unique.

findings.text: Feature list items are limited to 80 characters each.
findings.quote: Keep features short and scannable (up to 80 characters per feature)—focus on what merchants care about, not how it's built.

findings.text: You can list up to six integrations.
findings.quote: List up to six integrations that merchants will be most interested in.

findings.text: You can enter up to five search terms.
findings.quote: For search terms, enter up to five relevant terms using complete words (not partial) and limit to one idea per term

findings.text: Shopify recommends a 14-day free trial for paid apps.
findings.quote: Choose your primary billing method (Free to install, Recurring charge, or One-time payment) and provide clear pricing information in the designated section only. If you have paid plans, consider offering a free trial (we recommend 14 days).

findings.text: Create an app listing by selecting Shopify App Store as the distribution method.
findings.quote: To create a listing, select Shopify App Store as the distribution method.

findings.text: Set install eligibility criteria in the app submission form.
findings.quote: Set install eligibility criteria in the app submission form to reduce uninstalls and negative reviews from ineligible merchants.

findings.text: Public apps must use expiring offline access tokens for the GraphQL Admin API and REST Admin API.
findings.quote: Public apps must use expiring offline access tokens for the GraphQL Admin API and REST Admin API. Non-expiring offline access tokens aren't permitted.

findings.text: New public apps must be built exclusively with the GraphQL Admin API.
findings.quote: As of April 1, 2025 all new public apps must be built exclusively with the GraphQL Admin API.

findings.text: The app must authenticate using OAuth immediately after installation.
findings.quote: Your app must immediately authenticate using OAuth before any other steps occur. Merchants should not be able to interact with the user interface (UI) before OAuth.

findings.text: The app must redirect the merchant to the app UI after they accept permissions on the OAuth page.
findings.quote: Your app must redirect merchants to the user interface (UI) after they accept permissions access on the OAuth handshake page.

findings.text: Apps cannot be installed or initiated outside of Shopify services.
findings.quote: Apps must be installed and initiated only on Shopify services. Your app must not request the manual entry of a myshopify.com URL or a shop's domain during the installation or configuration flow.

findings.text: Apps must not use off-platform billing.
findings.quote: Apps that use off-platform billing cannot be distributed through the Shopify App store, unless you've been notified otherwise by Shopify. Your app must use Shopify App Pricing or the Shopify Billing API for all app charges and be free of billing related errors.

findings.text: Use optional scopes for scopes that are not required for all merchants.
findings.quote: For scopes that are not required for all merchants, we strongly recommend using optional scopes.

findings.text: Shopify recommends building embedded apps using the Shopify CLI.
findings.quote: Most apps are embedded, meaning they run inside the Shopify admin, and building one with Shopify CLI is the recommended path.

findings.text: Shopify managed installation handles scope updates and merchant approval automatically.
findings.quote: The installation method where Shopify installs your app and updates its access scopes without calling your app. You declare the scopes your app needs in its shopify.app.toml configuration file and push it to Shopify, which then handles the merchant's approval.

findings.text: The client secret must be kept server-side and never shipped in client code.
findings.quote: The client secret isn't: it proves a request comes from your app, so keep it server-side and never ship it in client code.

findings.text: You can no longer create apps directly in the Shopify admin.
findings.quote: The table above doesn't cover apps created directly in the Shopify admin, which Shopify pre-generates an access token for when the merchant installs the app. You can no longer create these apps

findings.text: Declare the scopes your app needs in its shopify.app.toml configuration file.
findings.quote: You declare the scopes your app needs in its shopify.app.toml configuration file and push it to Shopify, which then handles the merchant's approval.

findings.text: For apps running outside the Shopify admin, the merchant is redirected to Shopify to approve access.
findings.quote: The merchant is redirected to Shopify to approve access, then back to your app with a code that your app exchanges for an access token.

findings.text: Send the access token in the X-Shopify-Access-Token header on every GraphQL Admin API request.
findings.quote: Your app sends the token in the X-Shopify-Access-Token header on every GraphQL Admin API request.

findings.text: Shopify recommends building embedded apps using the Shopify CLI.
findings.quote: Most apps are embedded, meaning they run inside the Shopify admin, and building one with Shopify CLI is the recommended path.

findings.text: You must agree to the Partner Program Agreement and the Shopify API License and Terms of Use.
findings.quote: Ensure you agree to follow the terms outlined in the Partner Program Agreement and the Shopify API License and Terms of Use.

findings.text: Log in to your Dev Dashboard.
findings.quote: 1. Log in to your Dev Dashboard.

findings.text: Click Apps in the Dev Dashboard.
findings.quote: 2. Click Apps.

findings.text: Click the name of your app to navigate to the App overview page.
findings.quote: 3. Click the name of your app to navigate to the App overview page.

findings.text: Click Install app in the Installs section.
findings.quote: 4. On the app overview page, in the Installs section, click Install app.

findings.text: Select the development store you wish to use.
findings.quote: 5. Select the development store you wish to use.

findings.text: Apps that do not redirect to the OAuth grant screen upon installation will be rejected.
findings.quote: When the app is installed, it doesn’t immediately redirect to the OAuth grant screen

findings.text: Apps that return a fatal error after installation will be rejected.
findings.quote: The app returns a fatal error after installation

findings.text: Apps that do not re-install properly will be rejected.
findings.quote: The app doesn’t re-install properly

findings.text: Apps that switch between embedded and not embedded versions will be rejected.
findings.quote: The app switches between embedded and not embedded versions

findings.text: Apps with broken or unusable interfaces upon installation will be rejected.
findings.quote: The app interface is broken and unusable upon installation

findings.text: Apps with web errors such as 404s, 500s, and 300s will be rejected.
findings.quote: The app has web errors such as 404s, 500s, and 300s

findings.text: Apps submitted without proper testing instructions or credentials will be rejected.
findings.quote: The app is submitted without proper testing instructions or credentials

findings.text: Apps that are not in a stable state will be rejected.
findings.quote: App must be a finished product and in a stable state

findings.text: Online store apps not using theme app extensions will be rejected.
findings.quote: The app isn't using theme app extensions.

findings.text: Online store apps not showing widgets properly will be rejected.
findings.quote: The app isn't showing widgets properly on the storefront

findings.quote: 1. Log in to your Dev Dashboard.

findings.quote: 2. Click Apps.

findings.quote: 3. Click the name of your app to navigate to the App overview page.

findings.quote: 4. On the app overview page, in the Installs section, click Install app.

findings.quote: 5. Select the development store you wish to use.

findings.text: App installation fails if it does not immediately redirect to the OAuth grant screen.
findings.quote: When the app is installed, it doesn’t immediately redirect to the OAuth grant screen

findings.text: App fails review if it returns a fatal error after installation.
findings.quote: The app returns a fatal error after installation

findings.text: App fails review if it does not re-install properly for merchants who have previously installed it.
findings.quote: The app doesn’t re-install properly

findings.text: Declare the required access scopes in the shopify.app.toml file.

findings.quote: Expiring offline access tokens are required for public apps that call the GraphQL Admin API.

findings.text: Online access tokens are tied to the staff member session, while offline tokens persist across sessions.
findings.quote: Online access tokens are tied to the staff member who opened your app, and their lifespan is limited to that user's session.

findings.text: You can initialize a new app using the Shopify CLI.
findings.quote: Initialize new apps, themes, and headless storefronts in an instant with the latest Shopify CLI. A single command installs all the dependencies you need, including the CLI itself, so you can dive straight into development.

findings.text: Shopify recommends a 14-day free trial for paid apps.

findings.text: Shopify recommends adding the App Bridge script tag to the head of each document.
findings.quote: We recommend adding it to the of each document of your app or as the first script element.

findings.text: Shopify recommends using optional scopes for scopes not required for all merchants.
findings.quote: For scopes that are not required for all merchants, we strongly recommend using optional scopes.

findings.text: The Shopify app review team verifies all requirements after you submit.
findings.quote: The Shopify app review team still verifies all requirements after you submit.

findings.text: The Shopify app review team can reject an app at their discretion if it doesn't meet the set standards.
findings.quote: The Shopify App Review team can reject an app at their discretion if it doesn't meet the set standards.

findings.text: After the Shopify app review team completes their review of an appeal to change app categorization, they'll send a response, whether it's approved or rejected.
